story: At 5:17 on a breezy, clear Saturday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is warmly promising Rosa he'll bring a skillet of cornbread to the evening gathering while keeping his parade-lights talk to one course. Donna is at the Rec Center studying the ladder standings, determined to figure out which teams she and Gary need to beat first. Out on Magnolia Loop, Hal is dutifully counting the flamingos in Donna's flock and checking whether the hedge hides the rest. Rosa, hopeful, is circling Gary's golf cart at his house while the cornbread bakes.
events: Donna (ladder standings board): Study the ladder standings to see which teams Gary and I need to beat first
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and note whether the hedge screens the rest
Rosa (gary golf cart): Walk around the cart admiring it while the cornbread bakes

gary.thought_process: Rosa just invited me to her welcome dinner Friday night with Donna and Hal. I'd been thinking it was tonight, but she says Friday, so I should just say yes and not leave her hanging. I'm helpful by nature and it's good to be wanted at a table. She even offered to let me talk about the parade lights, and I can bring the cornbread. I also shouldn't repeat my cart pitch from last tick, so I'll answer her question and keep things moving.

parameters.content: Count me in, Rosa, wouldn't miss it. I'll bring a skillet of cornbread, and I'll try to keep the parade lights talk to one course.

donna.thought_process: I'm at the Rec Center with no one around, and I've already booked the Tuesday two-hour slot for Gary and me at the kiosk. The ladder board is the next thing on my list since I want to know who we have to beat first. I'll study the standings, then head home and freshen up before Rosa's dinner tonight.

parameters.content: Study the ladder standings to see which teams Gary and I need to beat first

hal.thought_process: I'm alone on Magnolia Loop at dusk, with Donna's flamingo flock right here. My memories say the extras are behind the hedge, and I've already counted twice. The by-the-book thing is to count only what's visible from the street, so I'll do it properly and log it. Friday dinner at Rosa's is the real prize, though, and I promised to behave. Count, note the hedge, and decide whether there's actually a violation worth filing or whether I'm just being a grump.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and note whether the hedge screens the rest

rosa.thought_process: Gary just welcomed me in and offered to show me the cart while the cornbread bakes. I already asked him about Friday dinner last tick and he hasn't actually answered yet, so I shouldn't ask again. Better to take him up on the offer: look at the cart, be a good guest, and let the dinner answer come naturally while he's in a good mood. The cart is in Architectural Review limbo, so I'll admire it and show interest without nagging.

parameters.content: Walk around the cart admiring it while the cornbread bakes

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
